prompt: Summarize this scientific methods section into a single paragraph a journalist could use, explicitly flagging any part of the methodology that limits how strongly the results can be generalized: 'Participants (n=45, convenience sample from a single university) completed a 6-week intervention involving daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions via a mobile app. Self-reported stress levels were measured using the PSS-10 scale at baseline and post-intervention. No control group was used due to resource constraints; instead, a within-subjects pre-post design was employed.'

response_text: In a recent study tracking 45 university students who used a daily 10-minute mindfulness mobile app for six weeks, participants reported a decrease in stress based on the PSS-10 scale from the beginning to the end of the intervention. However, the strength and real-world applicability of these findings are severely limited: because the study relied on a small, non-random convenience sample from a single university and lacked a control group—utilizing only a pre-post design due to resource constraints—it is impossible to rule out outside factors or a placebo effect as the actual drivers of the stress reduction.
